findings.what: AC4 states three distinct comparison rules: MTD gets 'the elapsed prior-month interval capped at month-end'; a HISTORIC (already-complete) month gets 'the prior FULL month'; balances get 'the preceding month-end'. The door implements only one formula for both the MTD and the historic-month cases (v_prev_stop = least(v_prev_start + (v_as_of - v_start) days, v_prev_start + 1 month - 1 day)), with no branch on whether the read covers a complete calendar month. For a historic month whose length is SHORTER than the immediately preceding month (Feb after Jan, Apr after Mar, Jun after May, Sep after Aug, Nov after Oct - five of twelve month pairs, recurring every year), the elapsed-day count equals the SELECTED month's own (shorter) length, so v_prev_stop truncates the prior month at that shorter length instead of using it in full - silently dropping the tail days of the prior month from the profit/income/expense comparison baseline.
findings.failure_scenario: clara.get_client_financial_pack(client, null, '2026-02-01') (a plain historic-month read of February 2026, 28 days) computes v_prev_start=2026-01-01 and, per the current formula, v_prev_stop=2026-01-28 - NOT 2026-01-31. Any January income/expense posted on the 29th-31st is silently excluded from the 'prior month' comparison baseline, so profit.comparison.value_cents / delta_cents / delta_pct (and the same for income and expense) are wrong for every February, April, June, September and November read of this door, every year, with no error, no distinct coverage/status flag, and no test catching it - exactly the class of silent-wrongness trap the ticket's own risk section names as requiring both a prosrc assertion and a behavioural cell.
findings.evidence: Live SQL on the assigned rig (clara_660) evaluating the pack's own v_prev_start/v_prev_stop expressions verbatim: for (v_start=2026-02-01, v_as_of=2026-02-28) -> v_prev_stop=2026-01-28 (not 2026-01-31); for (v_start=2026-04-01, v_as_of=2026-04-30) -> v_prev_stop=2026-03-30 (not 2026-03-31); for (v_start=2026-03-01, v_as_of=2026-03-31) -> v_prev_stop=2026-02-28 (correct, but only because March, 31 days, is LONGER than February, so the existing p660.pack.mtd_comparison_capped test cell - which uses exactly this March/February pair - cannot distinguish the two formulas and passes either way). The only comparison-interval cells in packages/db/tests/client-financial-pack.test.mjs are p660.pack.mtd_comparison_capped (uses month='2026-03-01', the case where the bug is invisible) and p660.pack.zero_denominator+sign_change (no historic-month-shorter-than-predecessor case either). brief-660.md:275 states the AC4 wording ('history with the prior full month') verbatim; the migration's own header/comment at 0232:1065-1067 mislabels the shared formula as an 'MTD run', which is what let the historic-month case go unexamined.
findings.fix: Branch v_prev_stop on whether the read covers a COMPLETE calendar month (v_as_of = v_month_end) rather than applying the elapsed-day formula unconditionally: when v_as_of = v_month_end, set v_prev_stop := (v_prev_start + interval '1 month' - interval '1 day')::date unconditionally (the full prior month, per AC4's 'history' rule); keep today's elapsed-and-capped formula only for the genuine in-progress MTD case (v_as_of < v_month_end). Add a behavioural cell exercising a historic month shorter than its predecessor (e.g. month='2026-02-01' with January data posted on the 29th-31st) asserting profit.comparison.period.end = '2026-01-31' and that the comparison sums those late-January entries - the counterpart p660.pack.mtd_comparison_capped's March/February pair cannot supply.

findings.what: DECISIONS.md Section3 states '#902's debt declaration stays untouched' and brief-660.md's Web section says to register the three new verbs while 'leave :361 alone'. The actual diff rewrites that exact array from a single-entry debt list to a four-entry one (the original get_client_work_pack string plus the three new #660 verbs), which is a textual edit at the named location rather than leaving it untouched.
findings.failure_scenario: Not a runtime defect - LANE_DECLARATIONS is structurally one entry per mock file, so a new verb served by the same file has nowhere else to register given the file's existing shape, and the original get_client_work_pack entry's content and meaning are unchanged. This is a spec-wording tension rather than a functional bug.

The worker's own final report (Assumptions Section, item 6) discloses this choice: 'did not touch #902's debt entry beyond extending the same lane's array in place.'

Worth a one-line note in the wave's reconciliation log so a future reader does not read brief-660.md's 'leave :361 alone' as violated without also reading the disclosed rationale.

findings.what: brief-660.md's TDD-seams list names three separate web unit test files: client-cash-summary.test.tsx, client-profit-summary.test.tsx and client-financial-charts.test.tsx. Only client-financial-charts.test.tsx was created (338 lines); it mounts the full ClientFinancialSummary composite and does exercise both child components' rendered output (exact money strings, empty/zero/unpublished/denied states), but the file-per-component split the brief specified was not followed, and this consolidation is not named as an assumption or residual in the final report (unlike the golden-fixture-corpus consolidation, which was disclosed as Assumption 2).
findings.failure_scenario: None observed - behavioural coverage of both components appears substantively present via the composite test file. The gap is documentation/traceability: a reviewer searching for client-cash-summary.test.tsx by the name the brief promised will not find it and has to discover the actual coverage lives elsewhere.
findings.evidence: brief-660.md Section4 web-unit list names all three files by name; git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat -- 'apps/web/components/firm/client-home/*' shows only client-financial-charts.test.tsx (338 lines) among the test files, with client-cash-summary.tsx (118 lines) and client-profit-summary.tsx (117 lines) carrying no sibling test file; client-financial-charts.test.tsx:21-24 imports ClientFinancialSummary (the composite) and its test names (grepped) cover exact money strings, table fallback, pre-coverage, partial month, empty/zero/unpublished/denied, unmarked-history, drilldown and malformed-period.
findings.fix: No functional fix required. A one-line addition to the final report's Assumptions section naming the consolidation (parallel to how Assumption 2 already discloses the golden-fixture-corpus consolidation) would close the traceability gap.

findings.what: Every other file under apps/web/components/ui/ imports the class-name helper as `import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"` (the alias components.json declares under aliases.utils). The CLI-generated chart.tsx instead imports `import { cn } from "cn"`, pulling in a new, otherwise-unused npm package (cn@0.3.0, confirmed resolved in pnpm-lock.yaml) rather than the project's existing utility.
findings.failure_scenario: None - cn@0.3.0 is a real, trivial, dependency-free package and resolves correctly (pnpm typecheck/lint/build all green). This is a style/consistency note, not a defect.
findings.evidence: grep across apps/web/components/ui/*.tsx: 18 files import cn from "@/lib/utils"; chart.tsx alone imports from "cn". pnpm-lock.yaml:3575,10099 confirms cn@0.3.0 resolves with no sub-dependencies. This is exactly what D19.c's own measured dry run predicted ('deps cn + recharts@3.8.0') and what the final report's step 3 confirms was installed verbatim without further hand-editing of the generated file - consistent with the brief's mechanical, no-hand-edit ui:add procedure.
findings.fix: No action required against this ticket's own procedure (D19.c forbids hand-editing the guarded install beyond the four measured steps). Worth a follow-up decision at the orchestrator level: either accept `cn` as a second, permanent class-name-merge dependency going forward, or map the shadcn `cn` registry dependency to the project's `@/lib/utils` alias so future `ui:add` installs stay consistent with the other 18 files.
